chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Dawud narrated from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Bunan, from Abu al-Tahir (meaning al-Warraq), from al-Hajjāl, from more than one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"The soil from the grave of al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) [is valid for use] for ten miles."

key_terms.التُّرْبَةُ: The soil or earth, specifically referring to the clay used for prostration in Shia jurisprudence
key_terms.عَشَرَةُ أَمْيَالٍ: Ten miles, indicating the geographical limit of validity
key_terms.قَبْرِ الْحُسَيْنِ: The grave of al-Husayn ibn Ali

ai.seo_question: What is the valid radius for using Turbat al-Husayn?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* defines the sacred radius of ten miles around the shrine of Imam al-Husayn (AS), establishing the authenticity of its soil (turba) for ritual and medicinal use. This geographical demarcation underscores the theological significance of Karbala as a sanctified space, linking the physical earth to spiritual blessings (barakah) in Shia devotional practice.
